photo.title: photographic print (black and white); postcard
Posed group of men and boys outside brush shelter in clearing. Some have cicatrisation on their bodies; some are smoking pipes; some wear European clothing. [LM 10/2/2009]
Man holding two spears; wearing body paint and arm, head and neck ornaments. Forest background. [LM 27/4/2009]

Special fire on ceremonial ground for cooking 'kolamma' (yams) during 'Yam' initiation ceremony.  Old man lighting fire on earth mound and large group of men standing around it. [Poor photographs, taken in heavy rain] [LM 24/3/2009]

Group of ten men processing in a line through the forest during the 'Yam' Initiation Ceremony.  The men are decorated with white pipe clay and down on hair, face and bodies, and all carry sticks. (The same men can be seen in 1998.172.27.1) [LM 24/3/2009]
Men dancing and leaping (one caught in mid-air) around 'pukamani' (grave posts) in forest clearing, with the grave-posts just visible in the distance. [EE 2/1990]
Men dancing and leaping (one caught in mid-air) around 'pukamani' (grave posts), with the grave-posts just visible in the distance. [EE 2/1990]

Grave post dance on decorating ground. Men, many decorated with body paint, are dancing and watching others in a clearing in which are tall, carved and painted pukamani (grave posts). [EE 2/1990]

The same group may be seen in 1998.174.18.1. [JD 16/08/2006]

The removal? of large carved and painted pukamani (grave posts) from the decorating ground by men decorated with white body-paint.  Group of women and children watching from left of decorating ground. [EE 2/1990]

Full-length frontal view of two Tiwi women wearing painted bark mourning armlets, long tassel-string aprons and carrying gum leaves. Textile items (?European garments) on ground behind them. Trees in background. The same women can be seen in 1998.174.29.2. [LM 14/4/2009]

Full-length rear view of two Tiwi women with scarification on buttocks and wearing painted bark mourning armlets, long tassel-string aprons and carrying gum leaves. Textile items (?European garments) on ground in front of them. Trees in background. The same women can be seen in 1998.174.29.1. [LM 14/4/2009]
Painted pukamani (grave posts) at decorating ground; men standing around the posts. [LM 14/4/2009]
Rear view of two women standing on a beach, showing the cicatrices on their backs. One woman wears a necklace and a fabric skirt; the other wears armbands. [LM 17/3/2009]
Bathurst Island jetty and corrugated iron building.  Seven dugout canoes on beach with groups of Aboriginals sitting against them, and one wooden dinghy. Fenced area in background. [LM 10/3/2009]
A man decorating a second standing man with body decoration. A third man stands alongside looking away and holding weapons.
Posed group of young men wearing face and body paint, some with arm ornaments and scarification. Some wear textile loincloths. Trees in background. [LM 3/2/2009]

Group of men and  boys processing in a line through the forest during the 'Yam' Initiation Ceremony.  The men are decorated with white pipe clay and down on hair, face and bodies, and all carry sticks. (The same men appear in 1998.172.27.2.) [LM 24/3/2009]

Group of men, some carrying sticks, singing and walking round ceremonial fire in 'yam' initiation ceremony, whilst yams are roasted. Others shelter from the rain in two bark shelters in the left foreground. [LM 24/3/2009]

Special fire on ceremonial ground for cooking  'kolamma' (yams) during 'Yam' initiation ceremony.  Old men placing wood around mound where fire is lit while large group of men walk round it, many carrying long sticks. [Poor photograph, taken in heavy rain] [LM 24/3/2009]
Man, decorated with white body paint, dancing around fire during mourning ceremonies.  A group of men dance in response on the other side of fire. Trees in background. [LM 14/4/2009]

Men dancing around 'pukamani' (carved and painted grave posts) in forest clearing. The men are running up and hurling spears to drive the spirit 'Mapuditti' into the grave, while women look on from the right.  [LM 14/4/2009]
Men performing the Buffalo dance around the 'pukamani' (grave posts), with the grave-posts just visible. [EE 2/1990]

Grave post dance on decorating ground. Men, many decorated with white paint, are dancing and watching others in a clearing, in which are tall, carved and painted pukamani (grave posts).[EE 2/1990]

The same group may be seen in 1998.174.18.2.   [JD 16/08/2006]
Three people seated by old grave with 'pukamani' posts, two of which still have stringy-bark bags, used to store food during mortuary ritual, on top [poor photo]. [EE 2/1990]
Closing scenes of the memorial dance around 'pukamani' posts at grave. Men with body paint leaning against posts.[EE 2/1990]
Painted pukamani (grave posts) at decorating ground, before erection on graves, men running round the posts [EE 2/1990]
Men dancing around painted pukamani (grave posts) at decorating ground. [EE 2/1990]
Posed group of three men with cicatrisations, wearing face and body paint and head, groin, neck, arm and chest ornaments. One holds a spearthrower. Trees in background. [LM 3/2/2009]
Posed group of men with cicatrisations, wearing body paint and carrying spears. Trees in background. [LM 3/2/2009]
Men and boys digging holes for 'pukamani' mortuary posts. Several of the men wear body paint. [LM 17/2/2009]
Profile of a seated man, wearing European shorts. His hair, face and the cicatrices on his upper arms have been painted for the pukamani ceremony. [LM 17/3/2009]
Group of men, women and children in dugout canoe, some wearing European clothing. Bathurst Island is on the horizon; mangroves in middle distance. [LM 22/4/2009]
Group of men, ?making a bark canoe. Some wear European clothing. Trees in background. [LM 22/4/2009]
Group sitting outside bark-walled building in ?government settlement, wearing European clothing and making straw hats. [LM 22/4/2009]
Men and boys digging holes for 'pukamani' mortuary posts. Several of the men wear body paint. [LM 17/2/2009]
View across Apsley Strait to Bathurst Island. In the foreground are two boys in a dugout canoe with a dog in front of them; two other small boats are moored further out on the water. [LM 22/4/2009]
Group of men shaping a log in forest; women and children in the background. [LM 22/4/2009]
Posed group of men seated on ground in characteristic postures. Trees in background. [LM 3/2/2009]
Posed group of women and children holding pieces of bark in front of them for modesty. Background of trees; another woman is visible in the distance. [LM 3/2/2009]
Men with cicatrisation, body and hair paint (pipe clay), plucking out beard hair during 'yam' ceremony. [LM 24/3/2009]
Fire around which men dance during mourning ceremonies.  Semi-circle of men (cropped from top) stand on far side of fire. [LM 14/4/2009]

Men and boys digging holes for painted pukamani (grave posts) at a grave.   The men are decorated with white body paint and sit on the ground.  Old pukamani (grave posts) are in situ in background.  [EE 2/1990]
Newly painted 'pukamani' (grave posts) awaiting erection on graves, attended by small group of men and boys. [LM 14/4/2009]
Dancing around 'pukamani' posts newly erected at grave. [EE 2/1990]
Painted pukamani (grave posts) at decorating ground, before erection on graves, with men standing in semi-circle opposite them [EE 2/1990]
Four Aboriginal men in dugout canoe on water.  One man stands in the prow holding a spear.  Melville Island in background. [JD 4/8/2003]
Rear view of Aboriginal man standing on beach, showing cicatrization on shoulder, back and buttocks. He wears an armband. [LM 10/3/2009]

Standing man facing right, he is holding a spear in his right hand that he is just about to throw. He is wearing a textile groin cover and his head, chest, arms and thighs are decorated in white clay paint
